title: Company-wide policies and processes - Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for people managers, engineering and product leads, finance, and security.

Scope and purpose

- Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and approved vendors that interact with Redwood systems or handle Redwood data.
- Purpose: Provide consistent controls, clear approval paths, and practical checklists to minimize risk and reduce operational friction.

1) Access and permissions (RBAC & onboarding/offboarding)

Objective: Grant least-privilege access required for job function, ensure timely removal of access, and maintain an auditable trail.

Key policies:
- Principle: All access is granted on the principle of least privilege and is time-bound by default.
- Role definitions: Teams maintain an approved role-to-permission mapping in the Permissions Catalog (see related page: confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth).
- Provisioning: Managers request access using the Access Request form (People Ops tool). Requests must include justification, duration, and owner.
- Approval: Team owner + security approver required for production access. For high-risk systems (billing, secrets, production cluster), SOC (security-on-call) must be looped.
- Periodic review: Quarterly access reviews for production and sensitive systems; teams must attest via the Access Review workflow.

Onboarding checklist (technical):
1. Create core accounts (SSO, email).
2. Grant baseline role (as defined in Permissions Catalog).
3. Assign equipment and provisioning tickets.
4. Required training: Security 101, Data Handling, and Code of Conduct.
5. Confirm on-boarding completion in HR system within 7 days.

Offboarding checklist (technical):
1. Revoke SSO and cloud console access immediately on last day.
2. Rotate any credentials the leaver had access to within 24 hours.
3. Archive mailbox per retention policy.
4. Reclaim hardware and assets within 5 business days.
5. Log completion in offboarding tracker.

Emergency access
- Break-glass process: Short-lived elevated access can be granted through the emergency access workflow and requires post-hoc audit and justification.

2) Change management (infrastructure and software)

Objective: Reduce incident risk due to changes, ensure safe rollouts and rapid rollback paths.

Change types and approval matrix:
- Standard change: Routine, pre-approved (e.g., minor config updates) - documented in change catalog, no separate approval required.
- Significant change: Changes affecting production latency, availability, or security - requires PRD/Design + peer review + SRE approval and scheduled maintenance window.
- Emergency change: Unplanned production fixes - follow emergency change process with retrospective and RCA within 3 business days.

Required artifacts before production deploy:
- Design doc / ADR link (if architecture impact).
- Rollout plan (canary %, timeline, monitoring hooks).
- Backout plan and rollback steps.
- Test runbook / automated test coverage summary.

Deployment checklist:
1. Merge via CI with green test pipeline.
2. Deploy to staging, run smoke-tests.
3. Schedule canary (if applicable) and enable tracing/alerts.
4. Monitor SLOs for defined observation window.
5. Promote to full rollout if stable.

Change windows and maintenance communication:
- Routine maintenance: weekdays 02:00-06:00 UTC preferred for minimal user impact. Communicate 48 hours in advance for changes impacting customers.
- Emergency maintenance: Communication as soon as incident triage begins; status page updates per incident comms policy.

3) Data management and classification

Objective: Protect confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data and comply with retention and residency obligations.

Data classification levels:
- Public: Safe for external publication.
- Internal: Company-private but low-sensitivity internal data.
- Restricted: Contains PII, customer data, or security-sensitive information. Stronger controls apply.

Handling and storage rules:
- Restricted data must be stored in approved systems only (see Data Storage Catalog). Use encryption at rest and in transit.
- Production datasets: Access via controlled pipelines; no direct copies on laptops.
- Local copies: Prohibited for Restricted data unless a documented, approved exception exists.

Retention and deletion:
- Default retention: Internal data 3 years, Restricted data per contractual/regulatory requirements (typically 7 years unless specified).
- Deletion requests: Follow Data Subject Request procedure for applicable jurisdictions; Data Privacy team owns the process.

Data incidents and breach reporting:
- Any suspected data exposure is a security incident and must be reported to security@redwood.com immediately and followed up through incident response runbook.

4) Procurement and expenses

Objective: Ensure oversight, vendor selection based on cost and compliance, and clear reimbursement procedures.

Procurement workflow:
1. Request: Submit Purchase Request in Procurement system with vendor, justification, budget code, and estimated cost.
2. Approval thresholds: Manager approval < $5k, Finance + Manager $5k- $50k, Exec approval > $50k. Contractual exceptions and evergreen cloud spend handled by Finance.
3. Sourcing: For contracts > $25k, at least two vendor quotes required unless single-source justified and approved.
4. Purchase order (PO): Finance issues PO after approvals; vendor onboarding requires security questionnaire and insurance confirmation for sensitive services.

Expense policy (employee reimbursements):
- Submit expenses within 30 days with receipts. Per diem and travel guidelines below. Non-compliant expenses may be rejected.
- Company card usage: Follow Card Policy; reconcile monthly with receipts.

5) Vendor management and security vetting

Objective: Manage third-party risk and ensure contractual and technical controls are in place.

Vendor lifecycle:
- Evaluation: Security and privacy questionnaire, reference check, and pricing evaluation.
- Contracting: Legal & Finance own contract negotiation; include data protection addenda and SLA terms for critical vendors.
- Onboarding: Register vendor in Vendor Registry, assign a vendor owner, and complete technical onboarding (API keys, network allowlists).
- Monitoring: Quarterly vendor health review for critical vendors; annual recertification for vendors handling Restricted data.
- Offboarding: Revoke keys, remove access, confirm return/destruction of data if required.

Technical controls required for vendors handling customer or Restricted data:
- Encryption in transit and at rest.
- RBAC or scoped credentials.
- Audit logging for data access.
- SOC 2 Type II or equivalent evidence preferred for critical vendors.

6) Travel policy and expenses for employees

Objective: Enable business travel while controlling cost and ensuring traveler safety.

Booking and approvals:
- All travel must be booked via the company travel portal or with approved travel vendors.
- Manager pre-approval required for all work travel. International travel requires EOR/HR notification for visa/immigration coordination.

Spending guidelines:
- Flights: Economy for domestic; premium economy/upgrade allowed for flights >8 hours with manager pre-approval.
- Lodging: Reasonable business-class hotels; per-night limits set per region in Travel Rate Card.
- Meals: Reasonable, with per-meal limits defined in Travel Rate Card.
- Incidentals: Ground transport must follow safety and cost-efficiency guidelines (shared rides encouraged).

Safety and emergencies:
- Emergency contact: Travel team and People Ops reachable 24/7 for escalations.
- Travel insurance: Provided for employees traveling on company business; register trip in travel portal.

Expense submission:
- Submit within 30 days with itemized receipts. Use Expense Code and attach trip approval. Cardholders must reconcile monthly.

7) Internal templates and sample artifacts

This section contains quick links and guidance for commonly used templates. Templates are stored in the Templates folder in Confluence and the company Google Drive. Examples:
- Access Request form (template) - includes justification fields and duration.
- Change Management Checklist (deployment, rollback steps).
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (VSA template).
- Travel Request & Pre-Approval form.
- Procurement Request & PO template.

Maintain templates:
- Owners: Each template has an owner listed in the Templates index; owners must review annually.
- Versioning: When a template changes, increment version and note change summary and reviewer list.

Operational roles and ownership

- People Ops: Owner for onboarding, offboarding, travel policy, and templates maintenance.
- Security: Owner for access controls, RBAC policies, vendor security reviews, and incident handling.
- Finance: Owner for procurement thresholds, PO issuance, and expense reimbursement rules.
- SRE/Platform: Owner for change management and production deployment standards.

Governance and review cadence

- Annual review: Full policy review once per year by People Ops with Security and Finance.
- Quarterly audits: Access reviews and vendor recertifications where required.
- Policy exceptions: Documented exceptions require written approval by policy owner and an executive sponsor.

How to use this page and next steps

- Use the embedded templates for requests and follow the checklists for any action. If you need an exception, open a Policy Exception ticket with justification and sponsor.
- Questions or improvements: contact People Ops at policies@redwood.com.

Appendices (quick references)

- Approval matrix table (also published as downloadable CSV in Templates folder).
- Contact list: Security on-call, People Ops, Finance approvals - located in the Ops directory.
- Links: See related pages above for technical runbooks and RBAC definitions.
